links.outcome: Output score distribution drift monitoring vs. pre-deployment reference, detection of mismatched configurations
links.effect: Matched-reference PCCs 0.975–0.998 with no significant chi-squared differences (p 0.346–0.853); unmatched references gave PCCs 0.364–0.825, showing the method flags deviations.
links.quote: The low PCC value found when an unmatched manufacturer is used for the reference shows that finding a difference could be the source of an alert, which would facilitate the detection of software malfunctions or deviations (such as an unsupported manufacturer or a version of the tool that is not suitable for the analyzed mammogram).

links.outcome: Detection of deviations in deployed AI score distributions
links.effect: Global PCCs were 0.998, 0.975, 0.995 and 0.994 with matched references, versus 0.374, 0.825, 0.707 and 0.364 with unmatched references; proposed deviation threshold: 0.95. Clinical accuracy was not measured.
links.quote: The PCCs between each center distribution and an unmatched reference were 0.374 for center US-1, 0.825 for US-2, 0.707 for US-3 and 0.364 for US-4.

links.outcome: drift in AI output score distributions
links.effect: PCCs between each center's AI score distribution and the reference ranged from 0.975 to 0.998, indicating the AI behaved as expected without drift.
links.quote: The estimated PCCs were 0.998 [min: 0.993, max: 0.999] for center US-1, 0.975 [min: 0.923, max: 0.986] for US-2, 0.995 [min: 0.972, max: 0.998] for US-3 and 0.994 [min: 0.962, max: 0.982] for US-4.
